notes: Read the web barrel line by line. It is a pure re-export barrel of twelve sibling modules in the same directory: L1 HighlightCard, L2 MiniStat, L3 BatteryPill, L4 DigestSkeleton, L5 WeekSelector, L6 SummaryHeroCards, L7 DrivingSection, L8 ChargingSection, L9 BatteryHealthSection, L10 AlertsSection, L11 WeekOverWeekSummary, L12 useWeeklyDigest. No DOM, browser HTML, Recharts, Leaflet, framer-motion, lucide-react, or old web UI is referenced by the barrel itself — only relative './Sibling' specifiers.

Kept the native barrel a valid JSX-free .ts module that re-exports the exact public names from the exact './Sibling' relative paths the web barrel uses, preserving names and ordering byte-for-byte so each future re-export is a drop-in. This follows the established native dlq-inspector/index.ts barrel idiom for a re-export barrel whose siblings are separate conversion targets.

L9 BatteryHealthSection is the only sibling already ported (apps/native/.../weekly-digest/BatteryHealthSection.tsx exists with a named `export function BatteryHealthSection`), so it is re-exported live: `export { BatteryHealthSection } from './BatteryHealthSection';` — public name and source path unchanged.

L1-L8 and L10-L12 reference sibling modules that are not yet native conversion targets in this file-by-file loop. Actively re-exporting the not-yet-created './HighlightCard', './MiniStat', './BatteryPill', './DigestSkeleton', './WeekSelector', './SummaryHeroCards', './DrivingSection', './ChargingSection', './AlertsSection', './WeekOverWeekSummary', './useWeeklyDigest' would fail `tsc --noEmit`. Per the conversion contract's native-safe/unavailable-state rule these eleven exports are explicitly deferred and documented inline (each kept as the verbatim web export line in a comment block) so the barrel grows by uncommenting one line as each sibling is ported. This was chosen over fabricating render-nothing placeholder components (which the engineering rules prohibit) and over fully porting eleven out-of-scope chart-heavy siblings; deferral also fails loudly later for any consumer that needs an unported sibling rather than silently rendering an unavailable state.

Verified no native code imports this barrel today (grep across apps/native/src) so the partial public surface is non-breaking. Gates run from apps/native: npm run typecheck; npm run lint -- --quiet; npm test -- --runInBand --detectOpenHandles.
